kai: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on qwen2.5 when requests switch from latin to CJK mid-session. latency spikes ~2.3x and KV cache lookups drop to 0 hits for a few steps :confused:

maria: ugh. repro script?

kai: quick log paste:```
# payload sequence: en->zh
step=124 latency=23ms kernel=fast_fp16 kv_hits=1024
step=125 latency=58ms kernel=generic_fp32 kv_hits=0
step=126 latency=55ms kernel=generic_fp32 kv_hits=0
```

sam: kernel switching to generic_fp32 is suspicious. Could be autokernel heuristics seeing a dim/stride mismatch after tokenizer changes.

nora: is tokenizer returning multi-token pieces for CJK or adding leading spaces? We saw earlier that tokenizer boundary variations blow up RoPE offsets.

kai: exact issue: tokenization returns different token lengths, and our KV indexing path computes rope scale bin based on token byte-length vs token count -> ends up invalidating cached prefix entries.

maria: that should not invalidate KV cache, only change subsequent step positions. We might be mis-detecting sequence discontinuity and flushing cache. Any logs on cache invalidation events?

kai: from runtime trace: `KV_CACHE_INVALIDATE(reason=token_boundary_change)` emitted right at switch. Stack: batching->kv_layer->tokenizer_adapter.

sam: oh wow we tag token_boundary_change when tokens look non-monotonic in length. That is too aggressive. Previously we only flagged if `abs(delta_tokens) > 16`. Someone tightened that to >2 in recent change.

nora: PR? who made change?

maria: PR #4872 (perf/kv-stability) by @nora last month — it added heuristics to prefer column-major kernels when token length changed. Intended to avoid wrong RoPE indexing but probably overcorrected.

kai: the overcorrection triggers kernel fallback (fast_fp16 -> generic_fp32) because the kernel selector sees layout mismatch between expected kv_head_dim and tensor stride. That explains slower kernel and 0 kv hits.

perf-bot: perf regression alert — qwen2.5 e2e latency +38% on lang-switch workload (traces: 1887659999). Threshold breached.

sam: action plan: 1) revert aggressive token_boundary_change threshold to previous (16). 2) add a non-destructive check: if token_boundary_change && cached_kv_size matches expected token_count, do not invalidate. 3) add unit test for CJK mid-session tokenization.

nora: agree. also we should log exact kernel selection reasons in more detail (include head_dim vs kv_head_dim, stride, dtype). Current logs just say `kernel=generic_fp32`.

maria: I can whip up a micro-benchmark: run a mixed-lang prompt with controlled token lengths and capture kernel selector decision matrix + nvprof counters. Will run against staging qwen2.5 image.

kai: please include these counters: `sm_efficiency`, `achieved_occupancy`, and `latency_per_token`. Also capture `kv_cache_hits` per layer.

sam: temporary mitigation: pin `--prefer-kernel=fast_fp16` for affected routes in Dedicated pools until we patch heuristics. But careful: if there really is a stride mismatch we could corrupt outputs. Only safe if we ensure kv_head_dim parity.

maria: on that note — I found a model metadata inconsistency: model manifest declares `n_heads=32` but `kv_head_dim` computed as `head_dim * 2` in our loader for qwen2.5_v2. There might be a mis-spec for earlier variants which the autokernel saw and tried to compensate.

kai: so root cause chain: tokenizer boundary change -> aggressive invalidation -> kernel selector sees mismatch (manifest vs computed kv dims) -> fallback generic kernel -> kv cache flushed -> perf regression.

nora: timeline: I can revert the threshold today and add a guard in kernel selector to prefer same-dtype kernels when possible. Will send PR and smoke tests.

perf-bot: note saved: add regression test under perf/smoke/lang-switch.

maria: suggestion: during model onboarding, run a quick kernel-dim verification step that asserts `manifest.kv_head_dim == loader.computed_kv_dim` and warn if off by >0. It caught a couple of Mistral regressions earlier.

sam: good. also add a tiny integration test where tokenizer toggles from latin->cjk and we assert `kv_hits` stays stable (no flush).

kai: owner: @nora for PRs. @maria to run profiling and attach nvprof outputs. @sam to draft hotpatch config for Dedicated routes. I'll monitor metrics dashboard.

nora: on it. PR incoming in ~2h. will mark as revert + fix.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: staging/qwen2.5/rollout-1887659999 -> canary at 1887663600 (manual approval required).

maria: posted initial nvprof tarball to the ticket: link=https://internal/redwood/perf/1887659999/nvprof.tgz

kai: thanks everyone. If we can avoid cache invalidation, we should get latency back to baseline.

sam: after fix let's run a 12h soak with mixed-lang traffic to be sure no flakiness.

nora: added notes to CHANGELOG and will include unit reproducer in `tests/eng-runtime/kv_token_boundary_test.py`.

kai: closing loop — set severity P2 for now. Will escalate if canary shows any issue. :thumbsup:
